<a id="link.pipe"></a>

### Local pipe and protocol 1

`link.pipe` · service · stage **merged** · evidence **proven** · health **works** · P3

A local-only named pipe the game opens when the bridge is enabled, with a per-session token, a user-only access list, newline-delimited JSON and an allowlist of methods, so host tools can talk to the running game.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.8.15
- **Commands:** `bridge.ping`, `bridge.info`
- **Config:** `[bridge] enabled`, `[bridge] request_timeout_ms`, `[bridge] max_requests_per_second`, `[bridge] idle_disconnect_seconds`
- **Code:** `native/src/core/PipeServer.cpp`, `native/src/core/Bridge.cpp`, `tools/bridge-lib.ts`, `tools/bridge-client.ps1`
- **Row S2:** pass (script-call check, 0.2.0 c31156a, 2026-09-26): First in-game run of the pipe and the script-call context.
- **Row S3:** pass (script-call check, 0.2.0 c31156a, 2026-09-26)
- **Tests:** `tools/test/mcp.test.ts`, `tools/test/catalogue.test.ts`
- **Limit:** Requests are capped at 64 KiB and 32 levels of nesting.
- **Limit:** A rate limit covers every request (20 a second, bursts of 40 by default); the tools pace themselves at 18 a second in bursts of 36 and retry a rate_limited refusal for up to 4 s.
- **Limit:** A connection that sends five malformed or unauthenticated requests is dropped; a client silent for 120 s is disconnected.
- **Quirk:** The security boundary is the Windows user at medium integrity: any process running as the same user can read the token and connect.
- **Quirk:** Clients open the pipe at the Identification impersonation level and check the server's PID against session.json before sending the token.
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#bridge-in-one-paragraph](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#bridge-in-one-paragraph), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#32-protocol-1](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#32-protocol-1), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#4-safety-model](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#4-safety-model), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#script-call-check-first](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#script-call-check-first)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="link.script-calls"></a>

### Game and script calls from native code

`link.script-calls` · service · stage **merged** · evidence **proven** · health **works** · P3

Every game or script function is called the way script code calls it, with a caller frame and a context that is never null, on the game thread, so native reads and writes don't crash the game.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0
- **Depends on:** [`link.pipe`](#link.pipe)
- **Code:** `native/src/plugin/ScriptCall.cpp`, `native/src/core/ScriptFrame.cpp`, `native/src/core/GameThreadQueue.cpp`
- **Row S3:** pass (script-call check, 0.2.0 c31156a, 2026-09-26): The call that crashed before the fix returned with tweak_marker 1.
- **Row S5:** pass (script-call check, 0.2.0 c31156a, 2026-09-26)
- **Limit:** Engine addresses the call needs are resolved at load; if the address library lacks one, every game method is refused for the session (script_calls_unavailable).
- **Unknown:** Is the script_calls_unavailable refusal path right when an engine address is really missing? Settle by: Only a game build whose address library lacks an address can show it; knowledge/runtime-access.md lists it as built, not confirmed.. Needs the game.
- **Docs:** [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#35-calling-game-and-script-functions-from-native-code](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#35-calling-game-and-script-functions-from-native-code), [knowledge/runtime-access.md#6-what-agents-can-and-cannot-do-yet](../../../knowledge/runtime-access.md#6-what-agents-can-and-cannot-do-yet)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="link.script-gate"></a>

### Script-layer gate across loads

`link.script-gate` · safety · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P3

The bridge makes no script call between the scripts detaching for a load and the next session's player attaching; while the gate is closed game.status answers loading from the plugin and other game calls are refused game_loading.

- **Version:** since 0.5.2
- **Depends on:** [`link.script-calls`](#link.script-calls)
- **Code:** `native/src/core/ScriptLayer.cpp`, `native/src/core/Dispatcher.cpp`
- **Row I2:** pass (session 10, 0.8.2, 2026-10-22): game.load through the gate.
- **Row I3:** pass (session 10, 0.8.2, 2026-10-22)
- **Tests:** `tools/test/batch8.test.ts`
- **Quirk:** Calls after a new attach but before the player attaches are never made; whether they would be safe is untested.
- **Notes:** Built after session 5's crash, when game.wait polled game.status just after game.load detached the scripts. Session 6 passed its load checks.
- **Docs:** [knowledge/game-crashes.md#23-calling-scripts-while-a-save-loads](../../../knowledge/game-crashes.md#23-calling-scripts-while-a-save-loads), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#10-open-questions](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#10-open-questions), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#session-10-checks-bridge-082](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#session-10-checks-bridge-082)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="link.observers"></a>

### One writer and read-only observers

`link.observers` · service · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **caveats** · P2

One exclusive writer connection plus a bounded pool of independent read-only connections, so a watcher or catch-up reader can follow the game while another tool drives it.

- **Version:** since 0.8.15, changed in 0.8.16
- **Depends on:** [`link.pipe`](#link.pipe)
- **Config:** `[bridge] max_read_only_connections`
- **Code:** `native/src/core/PipeServer.cpp`, `tools/api/command-api.ts`
- **Demand (holotable, needs, want 14, M6):** The headless service as a read-only observer (readOnly: true). The runner, the Story Engine and Holotable each want a slot, so please raise the default from 3 to 6 after measuring.
- **Row MC1:** unrun
- **Row MC2:** partial (borg-2, 0.8.16 c96779ee, 2026-10-25): In practice: a read-only catch-up client ran beside the MCP writer all session with no bridge_busy and no effect on the writer; the row was not run as written.
- **Row MC3:** unrun
- **Row MC4:** unrun
- **Row MC5:** unrun
- **Row MC6:** unrun
- **Tests:** `tools/test/multiclient.test.ts`
- **Limit:** 0 to 8 read-only connections (3 by default); a second writer gets bridge_busy.
- **Limit:** npc.pick, starting the recorder, game.saves, game.options.read and test.events with stims stay writer-only (read_only_connection).
- **Limit:** Half the shared rate bucket's burst is reserved for the writer; readers can't fill the last slot of the 16-slot game-thread queue.
- **Quirk:** Recorder, supervisor and input leases follow the writer: an MCP connection holding them keeps the writer seat, so a CLI writer gets bridge_busy (Borg 4).
- **Quirk:** Scheduling bounds are established offline, not measured game latency.
- **Could improve (value high, effort small):** 0.8.24 (claude/bridge-0824, de216d6d): per-connection request budgets for observers (20/s, burst 40 each; observer ceiling 160/s) and six slots by default; six 1 Hz readers measured 360/360 with writer latency unchanged
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#concurrent-observers-0815-candidate](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#concurrent-observers-0815-candidate), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#concurrent-readers-0815](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#concurrent-readers-0815)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-28

### Write gate, write classes and pause

`safety.write-gate` · safety · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P3

Every write is refused unless the plugin's config.ini allows writes and lists the command's write class; the in-game panel can pause changes, which only takes access away.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.8.12
- **Depends on:** [`link.catalogue`](#link.catalogue)
- **Config:** `[bridge] allow_writes`, `[bridge] allow_write_classes`, `[bridge] allow_creator_leave`, `[bridge] allow_live_pose`, `[bridge] allow_test_hooks`
- **Code:** `native/src/core/Dispatcher.cpp`, `native/src/core/Config.cpp`
- **Tests:** `tools/test/batch4.test.ts`, `tools/test/batch5.test.ts`, `tools/test/mcp.test.ts`
- **Limit:** inventory, save, showroom, player and act must be listed by name; inventory stays off in every package until the maintainer approves writes to V's inventory.
- **Limit:** Release packages ship with the bridge off and every switch off; only the dedicated test profile's -writes package allows writes.
- **Quirk:** Paused writes answer writes_paused; resuming gives back exactly what config.ini allows, never more.
- **Notes:** Exercised in every session that wrote to the game since the first (26 September); row-level verdicts are in the session write-ups, not mirrored here yet.
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends), [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#configuration](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#configuration), [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#test-build-only-features](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#test-build-only-features)

<a id="safety.save-lock"></a>

### The save lock

`safety.save-lock` · safety · stage **merged** · evidence **proven** · health **caveats** · P2

Every write first takes a save lock that blocks the game's own saves until a save loads, so a test change never goes into a save by accident; game.save refuses while it is held unless told otherwise.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.8.7
- **Code:** `native/src/core/Writes.cpp`, `redscript/XFRuntimeBridgeGame.reds`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, P4, M5):** Story writes without the save lock: a save-safe route for everything the Story Engine changes. Planned in XF Core as play mode (core.play-mode).
- **Row S6:** pass (script-call check, 0.2.0 c31156a, 2026-09-26): The first write took the lock (saving_locked true).
- **Row IC4:** pass (borg-1, 0.8.13 306fa3c4, 2026-10-24): Save anyway saved once and the lock came back; the checker's save_delta failed falsely (see quirks).
- **Limit:** The lock is released only by loading a save; the kill switch keeps it, since other changes may still be live.
- **Quirk:** game.save refuses first, with or without override_lock, while the bridge holds anything on V a save would keep (bridge_effects_active).
- **Quirk:** The refusal's headline lists every possible cause; only its detail names the real holders (Borg 1 friction).
- **Issue (medium, open, research/story-engine/runtime-requirements.md):** Fine for test sessions, not for a campaign: every bridge write blocks the game's saves until a load (Story Engine P4, DS-39).
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#bridge-in-one-paragraph](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#bridge-in-one-paragraph), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#b-the-save-lock-and-save-anyway-5-min](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#b-the-save-lock-and-save-anyway-5-min), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#input-and-choices-borg-mode-session](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#input-and-choices-borg-mode-session)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="safety.commit-tripwire"></a>

### The commit tripwire

`safety.commit-tripwire` · safety · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P2

A host tool watches the machine's free commit during heavy session rows and, under its floor, runs the row's off switch or hands the game back, so a memory squeeze stops the bridge before the game crashes.

- **Version:** since 0.8.10, changed in 0.8.22
- **Code:** `tools/commit-tripwire.ts`
- **Row G9r2:** unrun: The stim tap beside the tripwire.
- **Quirk:** The floor is 4 GB of free commit; a trip exits 3 and means memory ran short, not that the row failed.
- **Could improve (value medium, effort small):** Drop a stop-reason file the session driver prints on every later reply, so a trip is seen at once (Borg 4 friction).
- **Notes:** Borg 4 (26 Oct): free commit fell to 3.4 GB at 08:10 and the tripwire called session.handover; later writes were refused handed_over and the game did not crash.
- **Docs:** [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#process-notes-for-every-session](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#process-notes-for-every-session), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#318-bridge-0810-session-16s-findings](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-design.md#318-bridge-0810-session-16s-findings)

<a id="world.scene-read"></a>

### The raw scene

`world.scene-read` · sense · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P2

scene.read gives the active camera with calibration points through the game's projection, V, the NPCs near her (with their record's affiliation, type, archetype and crowd flags on request), showroom heads, photo-mode lights, sight-line rays, time, rain, menus and the HUD's choices.

- **Version:** since 0.6.0, changed in 0.8.8
- **Commands:** `scene.read`
- **Code:** `redscript/XFRuntimeBridgeScene.reds`, `native/src/core/Scene.cpp`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, S3, M4):** The people around V: record, archetype, faction, appearance, current activity or workspot, and crowd density. Wanted next: the entity template path.
- **Row SN1:** pass (session 15, 0.8.8, 2026-10-23): npc_detail: NCPD officers read NCPD, vendors Civilian with crowd true (this card's SN1 in the session 15 section, not the safety row).
- **Tests:** `tools/test/batch10.test.ts`, `tools/test/senses.test.ts`
- **Quirk:** Every read of a world object follows the world-object rule: entity-level natives only, the record name after a cast (session 7's crash).
- **Quirk:** The weather's name and photo-mode lights' own values aren't script-readable in vanilla.
- **Could improve (value medium, effort medium):** The NPC's entity template path: script can't turn a resource reference into a path or hash; it needs a native read of the record's resource flat.
- **Notes:** npc_detail was proven in session 15 (NCPD officers read NCPD, vendors Civilian with crowd true), per the Story Engine's requirements page.
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends), [knowledge/population-and-affiliations.md](../../../knowledge/population-and-affiliations.md)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

npc.spawn with out_of_sight picks a walkable spot V can't see; npc.release with dissolve removes an actor only once it is out of her sight.

- **Version:** since 0.8.8
- **Part of:** [`npc.actors`](#npc.actors)
- **Commands:** `npc.spawn`, `npc.release`
- **Events:** `npc.dissolved`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, V16, M5):** Spawn outside V's view and hearing; dissolve by walking away and despawning out of sight; join a scene mid-phase, posed, with no visible fast-forward (not built).
- **Row ND1:** pass (session 15, 0.8.8, 2026-10-23): Landed 12 m behind V unseen.
- **Row ND2:** pass (session 15, 0.8.8, 2026-10-23): The dissolve waited until V looked away.

<a id="npc.crowd-substitution"></a>

### Crowd substitution

`npc.crowd-substitution` · verb · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **caveats** · P2

npc.substitute replaces a plain passer-by of the street crowd with an XF actor of the same look, unseen: it holds the original still, spawns the actor at its spot once V can't see it, and hides the original only when the actor stands there; every failed swap gives the original back.

- **Version:** since 0.8.19
- **Depends on:** [`npc.actors`](#npc.actors)
- **Commands:** `npc.substitute`, `npc.release`
- **Events:** `npc.substitute_started`, `npc.substituted`, `npc.substitute_failed`, `npc.restored`, `npc.original_returned`, `npc.original_unreturned`
- **Code:** `native/src/core/NpcSubstitute.cpp`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, V17, M5):** Adopt crowd people into the simulation (route a: substitution with the same look), keep identity across reloads through the resident key and respawn parameters, release cleanly.
- **Row CRS1:** unrun
- **Row CRS2:** partial (borg-4, 0.8.22 1cd681c3, 2026-10-26): The swap ran, but the look fell back: asked for the original's creole_11 appearance, got a king_of_the_stoop one.
- **Row CRS3:** pass (borg-4, 0.8.22 1cd681c3, 2026-10-26): Swapped 19 m away out of V's view within 0.8 s; the maintainer saw nothing odd.
- **Row CRS7:** partial (borg-4, 0.8.22 1cd681c3, 2026-10-26): Released with restore as a despawn (not a dissolve); a fresh crowd person came 2.9 s later rather than the original.
- **Row CRS12:** unrun: Borg 4 saw the npc_busy, npc_protected and too_far refusals right, not the community refusal.
- **Tests:** `tools/test/crowd-substitute.test.ts`
- **Limit:** Lane-crowd walkers only: community NPCs are refused (community_npc), because a quest reservation can't be detected and the removal can't be undone.
- **Quirk:** restore leaves a fresh crowd person, not the original; acceptable for crowds.
- **Quirk:** resident.key is ours (a hash of record, appearance and spawn spot), not the game's.
- **Unknown:** Which of HideIrreversibly's effects remain until recycling; does AIJoinCrowdCommand return a spawned crowd person to the lanes; does the clone flee gunfire? Settle by: CRS6, CRS7, CRS14. Needs the game.
- **Could improve (value medium, effort small):** Count look fall-backs and widen the candidate appearance search (Borg 4).
- **Docs:** [knowledge/npc-direction.md#12-crowd-substitution-bridge-0819](../../../knowledge/npc-direction.md#12-crowd-substitution-bridge-0819), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#crowd-substitution-0819](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#crowd-substitution-0819)

<a id="incidents.witness-reports"></a>

### What V witnessed

`incidents.witness-reports` · sense · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P1

The bridge groups what the game's own systems raise (stimuli, deaths, combat targets, reprimands, vehicle thefts, combat and fear barks) into incidents and sends one passive witness.report per incident V saw or heard, with its id, kind, people, place and times.

- **Why P1:** Story Engine S7 (M4): layer 3's gates need incidents linked to V. Borg 4 passed WI; the remaining WI rows run next.
- **Version:** since 0.8.20, changed in 0.8.21
- **Depends on:** [`recorder.source-recorder`](#recorder.source-recorder)
- **Commands:** `incidents.list`
- **Events:** `witness.report`, `witness.gap`
- **Code:** `native/src/core/Incidents.cpp`, `native/src/plugin/HandlersIncidents.cpp`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, S7, M4):** One passive report per incident V saw, heard or was told of, carrying the incident's identity, who took part, where, when and how V perceived it.
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, S1, M4):** Part of the world event feed: combat, deaths and crimes near V, grouped.
- **Row WI1:** unrun
- **Row WI2:** unrun
- **Row WI6:** unrun
- **Row WI10:** unrun
- **Row WI14:** unrun
- **Tests:** `tools/test/incidents0820.test.ts`
- **Limit:** 32 open incidents, 64 kept; 24 observations built a second (12 weak, 2 of one kind from one entity) and 40 accepted.
- **Limit:** 20 reports a minute with a queue of 64; a witness.gap event when even that is full; a 160 m gate before any work.
- **Limit:** Saw: a person other than V in the active camera's view within 80 m with no static geometry on the ray; heard: V inside the stimulus' own radius.
- **Quirk:** Was told is never sensed and never reported.
- **Quirk:** The game raises almost none of the Story Engine's incident kinds (no NPC theft, no stall collection); its only theft is V's own vehicle theft, so most incidents must be staged and declared.
- **Unknown:** Which WI rows did Borg 4's PASS cover? The findings record WI as passed without naming rows. Settle by: Name the rows in the next session's write-up.
- **Notes:** Autonomous build only; passive and read-only (nothing is sent into the game).
- **Docs:** [knowledge/game-events.md#13-incidents-what-v-witnessed-bridge-0820](../../../knowledge/game-events.md#13-incidents-what-v-witnessed-bridge-0820), [research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#witnessed-incidents-0820](../../../research/runtime/runtime-bridge-test-card.md#witnessed-incidents-0820)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#4-failure-semantics, M4):** Closed bookkeeping: a scene that gives up closes its declared incident, so it ends in exactly one report, unwitnessed outcome or gap.

<a id="photo.open"></a>

### Opening photo mode

`photo.open` · verb · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **caveats** · P3

photo.open presses the player's own photo-mode key in the game window (the one allowlisted input), only while the game window is in front and photo mode is allowed, then waits for photo mode.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.4.2
- **Commands:** `photo.open`, `photo.enter`
- **Code:** `tools/input/photo-key.ts`
- **Tests:** `tools/test/framing.test.ts`
- **Limit:** Only while the game window is already in front (focus: require); posted keys don't reach a background window, because the game reads Raw Input.
- **Limit:** Punctuation keys depend on the keyboard layout and are refused; an unbound or malformed binding is refused, never guessed.
- **Quirk:** photo.enter's quest-node route opens a restricted photo mode (first-person camera only, no V tab), so it refuses unless asked for by name.
- **Notes:** Seen working in sessions 4 to 6 and in Borg 1 (sendinput, the user's key).
- **Docs:** [knowledge/photo-mode.md#23-routes-to-the-full-photo-mode](../../../knowledge/photo-mode.md#23-routes-to-the-full-photo-mode), [knowledge/runtime-access.md#6-what-agents-can-and-cannot-do-yet](../../../knowledge/runtime-access.md#6-what-agents-can-and-cannot-do-yet)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="photo.frame"></a>

### Framing V

`photo.frame` · verb · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P3

photo.frame frames V's eyes, face, head and shoulders or full body at the window's centre from its lens's known pose, measuring through the game's own projection after every change and correcting with a refined Jacobian; any failure puts everything back.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.7.0
- **Depends on:** [`photo.state`](#photo.state), [`photo.camera`](#photo.camera)
- **Commands:** `photo.frame`
- **Code:** `tools/api/framing.ts`
- **Tests:** `tools/test/framing.test.ts`
- **Quirk:** A read straight after a change still shows the world from before it; framing reads until two readings agree (session 3).
- **Notes:** Seen working without drift in sessions 4 to 6; the target offsets are anatomical estimates until a session checks one capture per framing.
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends), [knowledge/runtime-access.md#6-what-agents-can-and-cannot-do-yet](../../../knowledge/runtime-access.md#6-what-agents-can-and-cannot-do-yet)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

- **Row SV8153:** pass (borg-3, 0.8.17 356f04c4, 2026-10-25): Yielded on mapped W (Borg 2) and on a raw mouse axis (Borg 3).

<a id="supervisor.plan-module"></a>

### Plans

`supervisor.plan-module` · service · stage **merged** · evidence **offline** · health **unknown** · P1

A plain-data, serialisable plan: steps with a precondition, an action, anticipated outcomes, branches, bounded retries, alternatives, a fallback and a deadline, roles and a shared blackboard, the failure ladder, and one report stream ending in exactly one closing report.

- **Why P1:** The Story Engine's scene execution sits on it, and the batch runner (the next session's ST batch) is its first consumer.
- **Code:** `tools/testing/plan.ts`, `tools/testing/fixtures/scene-a-pickpocket.plan.json`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#scene-execution-what-the-engine-needs-from-the-bridges-plan-layer, M4):** The engine decides what is true and what happens next; the plan decides how bodies carry it out, performs, observes and reports, and never changes the record.
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#1-what-a-scene-decides-at-run-time-and-against-which-signals, M4):** Anticipated outcomes map onto the scene's declared branches; an unanticipated outcome is reported as such and takes the fallback.
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#3-several-actors, M4):** A scene is a unit with a cast: joint beats, roles bound to actors, one blackboard per scene, one report stream per scene, up to 5 actors.
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#4-failure-semantics, M4):** The ladder: retry, alternative, drop a rung, dissolve, release; the truth once, no contradiction, a safe world, closed bookkeeping.
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#6-save-and-load, M4):** A load cancels every plan with one signal; start a scene at phase X at time t, not resume mid-plan; reports keyed by scene, plan and step so a duplicate counts once.
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, H5, M4):** The sequencer and frame-rate behaviours for staging beats (waits, conditions, per-step checks, undo).
- **Demand (session-runner, needs):** Rows with verdicts are plans: schema-3 session scripts run on the plan module.
- **Tests:** `tools/test/plan.test.ts`
- **Unknown:** Does the shape cover the start-at-phase entry point and idempotent reports keyed by scene, plan and step that the Story Engine asks for? Settle by: Review against the scene execution section with XF · Story Engine.
- **Notes:** Built with fake-clock tests and the Story Engine's scene A (the pickpocketing) on stub primitives. Executed host-side only today.
- **Docs:** [research/story-engine/runtime-requirements.md](../../../research/story-engine/runtime-requirements.md)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="supervisor.frame-rate-executor"></a>

### Plans executed in the game

`supervisor.frame-rate-executor` · service · stage **proposed** · evidence **none** · health **unknown** · P2

Run plans inside the game at frame rate, so the reflexes a scene needs (avoidance, facing, holding a bark its reading time, stopping when V blocks, aborting on combat, keeping inside the area) happen without the host, with beat-level reports within about a second.

- **Depends on:** [`supervisor.plan-module`](#supervisor.plan-module), [`supervisor.actor-entries`](#supervisor.actor-entries)
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#2-timing, M4):** Frame-rate reflexes in game; a report within about a second of the signal; a reflex may change how something looks, never what happened.
- **Notes:** The plan module is written as data so later in-game code can execute it; the supervisor's actor policies are its other planned consumer.
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="supervisor.primitives"></a>

### Scene primitives

`supervisor.primitives` · verb · stage **requested** · evidence **none** · health **unknown** · P2

The hand-written primitives plans are made of, parameterised by roles, places and timings with no story knowledge: approach and talk, a pickpocket's pass, paying at a stall, a shove, fleeing, following, waiting with an idle, leaving the area.

- **Depends on:** [`supervisor.plan-module`](#supervisor.plan-module), [`npc.direct`](#npc.direct), [`npc.speech`](#npc.speech)
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, runtime-requirements.md#5-authoring, M4):** The bridge owns the primitives and the executor; the engine owns composition. Fixtures: the market pickpocketing, the Friday collection, a warning under D-30.
- **Notes:** Scene A runs on stub primitives in the plan module's tests.
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="tooling.command-api"></a>

### The command API library

`tooling.command-api` · tool · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **works** · P2

CommandApi validates a command against its schema, audits writes, calls the bridge or a local handler and returns a plain result or refusal; the MCP server, the CLI, the session runner and the Story Engine's adapter all go through it.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.8.15
- **Depends on:** [`link.catalogue`](#link.catalogue)
- **Code:** `tools/api/command-api.ts`, `tools/bridge-lib.ts`
- **Demand (story-engine, needs, H1, M4):** A host-side route: the engine runs beside the game and drives it with catalogue commands, importing the command API in place, pinned to a bridge version.
- **Tests:** `tools/test/catalogue.test.ts`, `tools/test/mcp.test.ts`
- **Quirk:** One persistent CommandApi keeps the source connection across thinking turns (0.8.14).
- **Notes:** Every session since the first drove the game through it.
- **Docs:** [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/README.md#one-command-api-many-frontends), [projects/xf-runtime-bridge/docs/mcp.md](../../../projects/xf-runtime-bridge/docs/mcp.md)

### The MCP server

`tooling.mcp-server` · tool · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **caveats** · P3

A stdio MCP server on the official TypeScript SDK exposes the catalogue as tools (dots as underscores) with plain descriptions, permission and undo notes, --read-only and --allow class lists; its tool reference is generated from the catalogue.

- **Version:** since 0.2.0, changed in 0.8.22
- **Depends on:** [`tooling.command-api`](#tooling.command-api)
- **Code:** `tools/mcp/server.ts`, `tools/mcp-server.ts`, `tools/docs/mcp-reference.ts`, `docs/mcp-reference.md`

- **Tests:** `tools/test/mcp.test.ts`, `tools/test/mcp-reference.test.ts`
- **Quirk:** The server loads the catalogue at start: after a merge it must be reloaded, or newer inputs are refused (Borg 4: fighter_melee refused by a 0.8.16-era catalogue).
- **Quirk:** It keeps the pipe only while commands flow (closes after 3 s idle); while a scripted session holds its lock, every bridge tool answers that a session is driving the game.

<a id="tooling.batch-runner"></a>

### Batches of rows with verdicts

`tooling.batch-runner` · tool · stage **merged** · evidence **partial** · health **unknown** · P1

Schema-3 session scripts: each row ends PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL or SKIP with its evidence, one row's failure never stalls the batch; the runner sets the config.ini keys a row needs and restarts the game through MO2, keeps telemetry on every channel, halts fast on a significant bug and resumes.

- **Why P1:** The next session is the ST styling batch (st-styling.json, 34 rows in nine config groups) and the Borg 4 regression smoke, both generated for this runner.
- **Depends on:** [`tooling.session-runner`](#tooling.session-runner), [`supervisor.plan-module`](#supervisor.plan-module)
- **Code:** `tools/testing/batch.ts`, `tools/testing/config-ini.ts`, `tools/testing/telemetry.ts`, `tools/testing/loop.ts`, `tools/sessions/st-styling.json`, `tools/sessions/borg4-smoke.json`
- **Tests:** `tools/test/batch.test.ts`, `tools/test/batch-halt.test.ts`, `tools/test/review-0826.test.ts`
- **Quirk:** One persistent writer connection; handed_over or the commit tripwire stops the batch cleanly and the teardown always runs.
- **Quirk:** Key presses are guarded: only while the game is the foreground window, refusals recorded.
- **Notes:** Reviewed (H1 to H3, M4 to M15 fixed on the branch).
- **Docs:** [research/runtime/autonomous-testing.md#tier-6--one-yes-then-hands-off-session-orchestration](../../../research/runtime/autonomous-testing.md#tier-6--one-yes-then-hands-off-session-orchestration)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="core.plugin-host"></a>

### XF Core's plugin host

`core.plugin-host` · service · stage **planned** · evidence **none** · health **unknown** · P2

The bridge promoted to XF Core, a runtime base with no game features: plugins declared as a manifest plus redscript (and, first-party only, a native part through a C interface), checked at load, their scripts added only once accepted, with quarantine and a circuit breaker.

- **Demand (story-engine, needs, H2, M5):** A Story Engine plugin on XF Core: a manifest, redscript for game-side senses, verbs and watchers, and the engine as a companion process; the player installs XF Core and the plugin and nothing else.
- **Notes:** Phase C1 of the XF Core design: rename, flavours, plugin host, the native-part loader, bridge.hello, the session-file transition. Command names survive the move, so the MCP tools, CLI and scripts keep working.
- **Docs:** [research/runtime/xf-core-architecture.md#3-plugin-api](../../../research/runtime/xf-core-architecture.md#3-plugin-api), [research/runtime/xf-core-architecture.md#12-phased-plan](../../../research/runtime/xf-core-architecture.md#12-phased-plan)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26

<a id="core.lighting-plugin"></a>

### XF Lighting (the lighting mirror)

`core.lighting-plugin` · verb · stage **proposed** · evidence **offline** · health **unknown** · P3

Place an XF Studio lighting setup about V in photo mode with every light field set, follow V, remove it on exit and the kill switch, and read game lights back into the Studio.

- **Depends on:** [`core.plugin-host`](#core.plugin-host)
- **Code:** `tools/lighting/mirror-map.ts`
- **Demand (studio, wants):** A bridge-applied photo-mode rig that matches the Studio's lighting (banked until the product reaches 1.0).
- **Tests:** `tools/test/lighting-mirror.test.ts`
- **Notes:** Only the mapping exists, as an offline prototype (phase C6 of the XF Core plan).
- **Docs:** [research/runtime/lighting-mirror-design.md](../../../research/runtime/lighting-mirror-design.md)
- **Updated:** 2026-10-26
